newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Half of Swiss would rather leave past alone - poll.
newsitem.headline: Half of Swiss would rather leave past alone - poll.

text.p: Half of Switzerland's people would rather not dredge up the country's past as a wartime financial centre even though almost that many think its leaders at the time bore moral guilt, said an opinion poll released on Monday.

Swiss Radio's survey found 46 percent of those questioned believed the authorities had incurred moral blame for Switzerland's anti-Jewish refugee policy and business ties with Nazi Germany, but 51 percent wanted to let the matter drop.

Six out of 10 believed criticism of Switzerland's World War Two record from Jewish groups and other critics is overblown, it said, with 38 percent of these blaming foreign politicians, 35 percent foreign media and 26 percent citing Jewish circles for causing the row.

"This apparently defensive stance does not necessarily mean that the Swiss are not ready to confront the events of World War Two, but rather that they do not want the discussion forced on them "from abroad'," DRS radio said in a summary of the survey.

Acting in part on foreign pressure, the Berne government last month appointed a nine-member international panel of historians to review whether Switzerland acted honourably or cynically profited from the war, as critics allege.

The probe will focus at first on Swiss purchases of looted gold from the Nazis and Berne's policy of turning away thousands of Jewish refugees trying to flee to safety from Hitler. Berne billed Jewish groups for the upkeep of Jewish refugees let in.
While 46 percent said such behaviour made Swiss authorities morally culpable, 35 percent said officials had acted correctly and 20 percent had no opinion.
A joint panel of Swiss bankers and Jewish representatives is also searching for any unclaimed Holocaust accounts that may remain in Swiss banks despite two prior sweeps for such funds.
In all, 27 percent of survey respondents thought Switzerland was approaching the historical review appropriately. A fifth wanted a more intensive review.
The telephone survey of 1,089 people early this month found 53 percent favoured handing over to Jewish groups any unclaimed wealth found in dormant bank accounts.
Nearly one-third thought the funds should be given to charity, and 10 percent thought the money should stay in the banks or be given to the state.
